rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Al-Razi's associates argue that Abraham's plea to avoid idol worship shows that God alone grants abstention from prohibited acts.
rows.anchor: احتج أصحابنا بهذا الآية على أن أفعال العبد مخلوقة لله تعالى

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: His associates also infer from Abraham's request to establish prayer that God alone brings commanded acts about; Abraham thus affirmed that all acts are from God.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { رب اجعلنى مقيم الصلواة ومن ذريتى } يدل على أن فعل المأمورات لا يحصل إلا من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min is partitive: Abraham asks that some of his descendants be established in prayer, since God had informed him that some descendants would be unbelievers.
rows.anchor: كلمة ( من ) في قوله : { ومن ذريتى } للتبعيض ، وإنما ذكر هذا التبعيض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas takes duʿāʾ here to mean worship, citing Abraham's statement that he would leave those whom his people worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : يريد عبادتي بدليل قوله تعالى : { وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's request for forgiveness does not establish prior sin; it expresses reliance on God and abandoning hope except in divine favor, generosity, and mercy.
rows.anchor: والجواب : المقصود منه الالتجاء إلى الله تعالى وقطع الطمع إلا من فضله وكرمه ورحمته .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer is that permission to seek forgiveness for his parents was not known to be forbidden without revelation, so Abraham may have thought it permissible.
rows.anchor: الأول : أن المنع منه لا يعلم إلا بالتوقيف فلعله لم يجد منه منعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer identifies the parents for whom Abraham prayed as Adam and Eve.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أراد بوالديه آدم وحواء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third answer says Abraham's prayer for his parents was conditional on their becoming Muslims.
rows.anchor: الثالث : كان ذلك بشرط الإسلام .

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the phrase is the second object of warn and identifies the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { يوم يأتيهم العذاب } مفعول ثان لقوله : { وأنذر } وهو يوم القيامة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-ʿadhāb refers to the punishment already described: their eyes fixed and their heads raised.
rows.anchor: الألف واللام في لفظ { العذاب } للمعهود السابق ، يعني : وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warning means frightening people by mentioning harms.
rows.anchor: الإنذار هو التخويف بذكر المضار ، والمفسرون مجمعون على أن قوله :

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators agree that the day when the punishment comes is the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون مجمعون على أن قوله : { يوم يأتيهم العذاب } هو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim instead places the scene at the moment of death, when the dying person sees what is coming.
rows.anchor: وحمله أبو مسلم على أنه حال المعاينة ، والظاهر يشهد بخلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects Abū Muslim's timing: the request to return and the rebuke about denying departure fit the Resurrection, not death.
rows.anchor: لأنه تعالى وصف اليوم بأن عذابهم يأتي فيه وأنهم يسألون الرجعة ، ويقال لهم :

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim supports his reading by comparing the request for delay with the dying person's plea in the verse about giving charity before death.
rows.anchor: وحجة أبي مسلم : أن هذه الآية شبيهة بقوله تعالى : { وأنفقوا مما * رزقناكم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported view is that the wrongdoers ask to return to worldly life and make up what they neglected.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم : طلبوا الرجعة إلى الدنيا ليتلافوا ما فرطوا فيه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view is that they ask to return to a state of religious obligation, as shown by their promise to answer God and follow the messengers.
rows.anchor: وقال : بل طلبوا الرجوع إلى حال التكليف بدليل قولهم : نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their earlier oath denied moving from this life to another and from this abode to recompense, not ordinary change from life to death, youth to old age, or poverty to wealth.
rows.anchor: ومعنى : ما لكم من زوال ، لا شبهة في أنهم كانوا يقولون لا زوال لنا من هذه الحياة إلى حياة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke recalls the unbelievers' emphatic oath that God would not resurrect the dead.
rows.anchor: ومعناه ما ذكره الله تعالى في آية أخرى ، وهو قوله تعالى : { وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت }

words: وسكنتم في مساكن الذين ظلموا أنفسهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The former dwellers are Noah's people, ʿĀd, and Thamūd, who wronged themselves through disbelief and disobedience; seeing their fate should have prompted reflection, so failure to learn merits blame.
rows.anchor: يعني سكنتم في مساكن الذين كفروا قبلكم ، وهم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone who dies or is killed dies at the appointed term; it is mistaken to claim that someone can die before that term.
rows.anchor: دلت الآية على أن كل من مات أو قتل فإنما مات بأجله ، وأن من قال : يجوز بأن يموت قبل أجله فمخطىء

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: A hypothetical objection says the inference works only if the destruction in the preceding verse means death, not punishment of annihilation.
rows.anchor: فإن قالوا : هذا الاستدلال إنما يتم إذا حملنا قوله : { وما أهلكنا } على الموت أما إذا حملناه على عذاب الاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that if destruction includes death the inference is direct; otherwise the reason its punishment cannot occur early or late also applies to death.
rows.anchor: قلنا : قوله : { وما أهلكنا } إما أن يدخل تحته الموت أو لا يدخل ، فإن دخل الاستدلال ظاهر لازم

words: وقالوا۟ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِى نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلذِّكْرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After emphasizing threats to the unbelievers, God presents their objections to the Prophet's claim.
rows.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما بالغ في تهديد الكفار ذكر بعده شبههم في إنكار نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that revelation brought on a faint-like state, which they mistook for madness; other verses deny that he was mad.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنه عليه السلام كان يظهر عليه عند نزول الوحي حالة شبيهة بالغشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they thought his being a true messenger from God implausible and called him mad because his teaching seemed beyond reason.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنم كانوا يستبعدون كونه رسولا حقا من عند الله تعالى

words: وَقَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِى نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلذِّكْرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may have used the address sarcastically, as Pharaoh insulted Moses and Shuʿayb's people used praise ironically; the Qur'an also uses glad tidings ironically for punishment.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنهم ذكروه على سبيل الاستهزاء كما قال فرعون : { إن رسولكم الذى أرسل إليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the description means the one upon whom Reminder was sent according to his own claim and the belief of his companions and followers.
rows.anchor: الثاني : { وقالوا يأيها الذى نزل عليه الذكر } في زعمه واعتقاده ، وعند أصحابه وأتباعه

words: لو ما تأتينا بالملائكة إن كنت من الصادقين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They pressed their challenge by demanding that angels come to them if Muhammad was truthful.
rows.anchor: ثم حكى عنهم أنهم قالوا في تقرير شبههم : { لو ما تأتينا بالملئكة إن كنت من الصادقين }

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj say lawlā and lawmā are two forms meaning halla, used both in statements and in questions.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج : لولا ولو ما لغتان : معناهما : هلا ويستعملان في الخبر والاستفهام

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the mīm in lawmā replaces the lām in lawlā, as in the paired forms istawlā/istawmā.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : لو ما الميم فيه بدل عن اللام في لولا ، ومثله استولى على الشيء واستومى عليه

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī cites khalaltuhu and khalamtuhu for befriending someone, and khilī/khilmī for a friend.
rows.anchor: وحكى الأصمعي : خاللته وخالمته إذا صادقته ، وهو خلى وخلمي أي صديقي

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read nunazzilu with an active nūn and doubled, kasra-marked zāy; angels is accusative as the object and God is the subject.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم : { ما ننزل } بالنون وبكسر الزاي والتشديد

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim reads the verb as passive, with angels in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم : { ما * تنزل } عن فعل ما لم يسمى فاعله ، والملائكة بالرفع

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers attribute the act of descending to the angels themselves.
rows.anchor: والباقون : ما تنزل الملائكة على إسناد فعل النزول إلى الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the angels descended as demanded, the unbelievers would receive no respite, because legal obligation ends when angels appear.
rows.anchor: يعني : لو نزلت الملائكة لم ينظروا أي يمهلوا فإن التكليف يزول عند نزول الملائكة

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of al-Naẓm derives idhan from idh plus an, with hamza deletion; idhan signals an elided verb meaning they would not be reprieved when their request occurred.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( النظم ) : لفظ اذن مركبة من كلمتين : من إذا وهو اسم بمنزلة حين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preservation declaration confirms the Prophet's earlier statement that God sent down the Reminder to him, which prompted their mocking address.
rows.anchor: أن القوم إنما قالوا : { وقالوا يأيها الذى نزل عليه الذكر } ( الحجر : 6 ) لأجل أنهم سمعوا النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first-person plural is a royal form of majesty; a single monarch says we did or said something to magnify the act.
rows.anchor: فهذه الصيغة وإن كانت للجمع إلا أن هذا من كلام الملوك عند إظهار التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers the pronoun's return to the Reminder: God protects it from distortion, additions, and omissions, as other verses affirm its integrity.
rows.anchor: القول الأول : أنه عائد إلى الذكر يعني : وإنا نحفظ ذلك الذكر من التحريف والزيادة والنقصان

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An objection asks why the Companions compiled the Qur'an into a codex if God's promise already guaranteed its preservation.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل : فلم اشتغلت الصحابة بجمع القرآن في المصحف وقد وعد الله تعالى بحفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions' compilation was itself one of the means by which God preserved the Qur'an, appointing them to that task.
rows.anchor: والجواب : أن جمعهم للقرآن كان من أسباب حفظ الله تعالى إياه فإنه تعالى لما أن حفظه قيضهم لذلك

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī's associates argue that preservation proves the basmala belongs to the Qur'an at the start of every sūra; otherwise the text would be exposed to addition or alteration.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا : وفي هذه الآية دلالة قوية على كون التسمية آية من أول كل سورة

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: They add that if the Companions could be suspected of inserting text, they could also be suspected of omitting it, undermining the Qur'an's status as proof.
rows.anchor: وذلك يوجب خروج القرآن عن كونه حجة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ offers the alternative that the pronoun refers to Muhammad: God is his protector.
rows.anchor: أن الكناية في قوله : { له } راجعة إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والمعنى وإنا لمحمد لحافظون وهو قول الفراء

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī supports the Muhammad referent: mentioning the revelation and what was revealed makes its recipient an understood referent, as in the pronoun for Qur'an in 97:1.
rows.anchor: وقوى ابن الأنباري هذا القول فقال : لما ذكر الله الإنزال والمنزل دل ذلك على المنزل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the alternative, Al-Rāzī judges the Qur'an referent stronger and more faithful to the verse's apparent wording.
rows.anchor: إلا أن القول الأول أرجح القولين وأحسنهما مشابهة لظاهر التنزيل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One account says God preserves the Qur'an by making it miraculous and unlike human speech, so additions or deletions disrupt its order and are recognized as alien.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : حفظه بأن جعله معجزا مباينا لكلام البشر فعجز الخلق عن الزيادة فيه والنقصان عنه

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another account says God protected the Qur'an by making creatures incapable of producing a rival to it.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : إنه تعالى صانه

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another account says God prevented corruption by appointing a community to memorize, study, and publicize the Qur'an for as long as religious obligation remains.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : أعجز الخلق عن إبطاله وإفساده بأن قيض جماعة يحفظونه ويدرسونه ويشهرونه فيما بين الخلق

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another account says any attempt to change a letter or dot would be exposed by the community, even children correcting an eminent elder's slip.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : المراد بالحفظ هو أن أحدا لو حاول تغييره بحرف أو نقطة لقال له أهل الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No other scripture has remained free of copying errors and alteration, while the Qur'an remains protected despite the strong motives of heretics, Jews, and Christians to corrupt it; this is a great miracle.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه لم يتفق لشيء من الكتب مثل هذا الحفظ ، فإنه لا كتاب إلا وقد دخله التصحيف والتحريف والتغيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's continued preservation for nearly six centuries after God's prediction is knowledge of the unseen and another decisive miracle.
rows.anchor: وأيضا أخبر الله تعالى عن بقائه محفوظا عن التغيير والتحريف ، وانقضى الآن قريبا من ستمائة سنة

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī uses the preservation promise to refute some Imāmīs who claim the Qur'an acquired additions, omissions, or alterations.
rows.anchor: احتج القاضي بقوله : { إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون } على فساد قول بعض الإمامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī calls that proof weak and circular: Imāmīs could say this very preservation verse is one of the additions they allege.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن إثبات هذا المطلوب بهذه الآية يجري مجرى إثبات الشيء نفسه

words: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting the creation of the first human as evidence for a powerful, choosing God, the passage turns to God's command that the angels prostrate; all obeyed except Iblis.
rows.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما ذكر حدوث الإنسان الأول واستدل بذكره على وجود الإله القادر المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashar denotes a dense body that touches and meets; angels and jinn do not make such contact because their bodies are too subtle, and bashara is the outer skin of any animal.
rows.anchor: فالمراد منه كونه جسما كثيفا يباشر ويلاقي والملائكة والجن لا يباشرون للطف أجسامهم عن أجسام البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of God's forming Adam is shaping him in human form and bodily constitution.
rows.anchor: الأول : فإذا سويت شكله بالصورة الإنسانية والخلقة البشرية .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is arranging Adam's bodily parts through balanced temperaments and proportioned mixtures, as the verse about the human being formed from mixed fluid says.
rows.anchor: والثاني : فإذا سويت أجزاء بدنه باعتدال الطبائع وتناسب الأمشاج كما قال تعالى : { إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة أمشاج }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blowing is moving air through cavities in another body; the wording appears to imply that spirit is air, though the full account of spirit is deferred to 17:85.
rows.anchor: أن النفخ إجراء الريح في تجاويف جسم آخر ، وظاهر هذا اللفظ يشعر بأن الروح هي الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God attributes Adam's spirit to Himself as a mark of honor and distinction.
rows.anchor: وإنما أضاف الله سبحانه روح آدم إلى نفسه تشريفا له وتكريما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exegetical question is whether the prostration was truly directed to Adam or whether Adam served as its qibla.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك السجود كان لآدم في الحقيقة أو كان آدم كالقبلة لذلك السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may have addressed all heavenly angels, only some angels, or the angels of earth.
rows.anchor: أن المأمورين بالسجود لآدم عليه السلام كل ملائكة السموات أو بعضهم أو ملائكة الأرض

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some deny that the highest angels were commanded to prostrate to Adam, since the verse about those near God says they prostrate to God alone.
rows.anchor: من الناس من لا يجوز أن يقال : إن أكابر الملائكة كانوا مأمورين بالسجود لآدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general wording commands prostration to Adam, but the specific statement that the angels prostrate to God alone takes precedence over that general wording.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الخاص مقدم على العام

words: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in the command indicates immediate succession after God's forming and breathing the spirit, with no intervening delay.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الآية يدل على أنه تعالى كما نفخ الروح في آدم عليه السلام وجب على الملائكة أن يسجدوا له

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh call kulluhum ajmaʿūn emphasis after emphasis.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل وسيبويه قوله : { كلهم أجمعون } توكيد بعد توكيد

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says kulluhum rules out some angels only, while ajmaʿūn rules out their prostrating at different times and shows they all prostrated together.
rows.anchor: وسئل المبرد عن هذه الآية فقال : لو قال فسجد الملائكة احتمل أن يكون سجد بعضهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj prefers al-Khalīl and Sībawayh: ajmaʿūn is definite and therefore cannot be a circumstantial adverb.
rows.anchor: ولما حكى الزجاج هذا القول عن المبرد قال : وقول الخليل وسيبويه أجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators agree that Iblis was commanded to prostrate, while disagreeing over whether he was one of the angels.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في أنه هل كان من الملائكة أم لا ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a resumption answering an implied question about why Iblis did not prostrate: he refused and arrogantly resisted.
rows.anchor: استئناف وتقديره أن قائلا قال : هلا سجد فقيل : أبى ذلك واستكبر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer says the curse lasts forever; Resurrection is simply the farthest endpoint people commonly name, as in the expression as long as the heavens and earth endure.
rows.anchor: المراد منه التأبيد ، وذكر القيامة أبعد غاية يذكرها الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer says Iblis is condemned in heaven and earth until Resurrection but not yet punished; then punishment is so severe that it distracts him from the curse, making it seem to cease.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنك مذموم مدعو عليك باللعنة في السموات والأرض إلى يوم الدين من غير أن يعذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After presenting the ordered signs as proofs of a wise Creator and explanations of His blessings, the passage rejects worship of anything besides Him, especially inert objects.
rows.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما ذكر الدلائل الدالة على وجود القادر الحكيم على الترتيب الأحسن والنظم الأكمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator of the listed things cannot be equated with beings unable to create anything; even basic awareness shows worship belongs only to the greatest benefactor, never to lifeless idols without understanding, power, or choice.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أفمن يخلق هذه الأشياء التي ذكرناها كمن لا يخلق بل لا يقدر البتة على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The non-creators are idols: inert beings, although min normally marks rational beings.
rows.anchor: المراد بقوله : { من لا * يخلق } الأصنام ، وأنها جمادات فلا يليق بها لفظة ( من )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer to using rational min for idols is that unbelievers called them gods and worshipped them, so they are grammatically treated like rational beings.
rows.anchor: الوجه الأول : أن الكفار لما سموها آلهة وعبدوها ، لا جرم أجريت مجرى أولي العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation for min is stylistic matching with the preceding min in the phrase about the Creator.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثاني : في الجواب أن السبب فيه المشاكلة بينه وبين من يخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third answer means the Creator is unlike even non-creating rational beings, much more unlike idols; the question about idols' limbs shows their inferiority to living people, not that such limbs would make them worthy of worship.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المعنى أن من يخلق ليس كمن لا يخلق من أولي العلم فكيف من لا علم عنده كقوله : { ألهم أرجل يمشون بها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although an objector expects the comparison to be reversed, the wording stresses how impossible it is to equate the maker of immense benefits with contemptible, inert things in naming, worship, and reverence.
rows.anchor: والجواب : المراد منه أن من يخلق هذه الأشياء العظيمة ويعطي هذه المنافع الجليلة

rows.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
rows.claim: Some of al-Rāzī's associates infer that servants do not create their own acts: if creating anything made a being divine, humans who create acts would also have to be gods, which is false.
rows.anchor: احتج بعض أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أن العبد غير خالق لأفعال نفسه

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites answer that the verse contrasts the Creator of the heavens, earth, humans, animals, plants, seas, stars, and mountains with beings unable to create anything; this does not address a servant's acts.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة الجواب : عنه من وجوه : الوجه الأول

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites also say the verse establishes that a creator is superior to a non-creator and should not be equated with one in worship, but it does not make every creator a god.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة الجواب : عنه من وجوه : الوجه الأول

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their analogy is that a person with working legs is better than an idol unable to walk and should not worship the inferior idol; this does not make the person a god, just as creating alone does not imply divinity.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة الجواب : عنه من وجوه : الوجه الأول
